question: Which of the following Acts was replaced by the Competition Act 2002?
solution:
The correct answer is__** MRTP**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act (MRTP) of 1969 was replaced by the Competition Act of 2002: **
 
• The** Competition Act of 2002 governs Indian competition law and came into effect on September 1, 2009.**
 
• The Competition Commission of India **was established under this act to prevent activities that negatively impact competition in India.**
 
• The current competition law in India focuses on promoting competition, rather than curbing monopolies. 
 
• **The MRTP Act had several disadvantages, including:**
 
 
• Bureaucratic procedures
 
• Restrictions on business expansion
 
• Discouragement of foreign investment
 
• Lack of clarity in defining terms
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

​Competition Act, 2002:

 
• The Competition Act, of 2002 is a law that governs commercial competition in India.
 
• It replaced the erstwhile Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act, of 1969.
 
• The Competition Act aims to prevent activities that have an adverse effect on competition in India.
 
• The Act mainly covers these aspects;
 
 
• Prohibition of anti-competitive agreements.
 
• Prohibition of abuse of dominance.
 
• Regulation of combination (acquisition, mergers, and amalgamation of a certain size)
 
• Establishment of the competition commission of India.
 
• Power and functions of the competition commission of India.
